title: Determination of Nucleotide-Nucleotide and Nucleotide-Amino Acid Binding Interactions from All-Atom Potential-of-Mean-Force Calculations.
authors: Feito, Alejandro; Pedraza, Eduardo; Cuesta, Estefania; Castro, Alejandro; Rey, Antonio; Sanchez-Burgos, Ignacio; Collepardo-Guevara, Rosana; Tejedor, Andres R; Espinosa, Jorge R
one_liner_zh: 该文用全原子MD和PMF计算系统表征RNA核苷酸与蛋白氨基酸间的结合相互作用，为无序蛋白/RNA凝聚体中的PPI机制建模提供定量参数库，方法上属物理模拟且直接服务相分离互作机制。
abstract: Biomolecular condensates emerge from multivalent interactions between proteins and nucleic acids and are frequently modeled by using coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations. The parametrization of these models critically depends on atomistic data describing the underlying molecular interactions. In this work, we employ all-atom molecular dynamics simulations and potential-of-mean-force (PMF) calculations to investigate the landscape of interactions between RNA nucleotides and protein amino acids. We begin by characterizing nucleotide-nucleotide binding modes through canonical base-pairing analysis, observing notable agreement in the predictions from both the AMBER03ws and CHARMM36 force fields. Further rationalization of different nucleotide-nucleotide interaction modes involves the calculation of PMFs for ribose-ribose, phosphate-phosphate, and RNA tertiary interactions such as G-quadruplex formation. We also examine the effect of salt concentration on these interactions, finding a reduction in electrostatic self-repulsion for phosphate-phosphate binding upon increasing the ionic strength. Expanding our analysis to amino acids, we first benchmark the performance of both AMBER03ws and a99SB-disp force fields for describing pairwise amino acid interactions, and then, we evaluate different nucleotide-amino acid binding profiles. Our findings reveal a subset of amino acidsLys and Arg (positively charged), Asp and Glu (negatively charged), and Gln, Ser, and Asn (polar residues)that consistently engage with the nitrogenous bases of different nucleotides. Such binding is primarily mediated by hydrogen bonding and, in some cases, cation-pi interactions. Furthermore, we identify strong pi-pi stacking interactions with aromatic residues and phosphate-Arg contacts as key contributors to condensate cohesion in RNA-protein condensates. Our comprehensive analysis provides a detailed library of nucleotide-amino acid interactions, offering quantitative insights to inform coarse-grained model parametrization and deepening our understanding of condensate self-assembly, nucleic acid recognition, and phase-separation regulation at the submolecular scale.
abstract_zh: 生物分子凝聚体源于蛋白质与核酸之间的多价相互作用，通常通过粗粒化分子动力学模拟进行建模。这些模型的参数化关键依赖于描述底层分子相互作用的原子级数据。在本工作中，我们采用全原子分子动力学模拟和平均力势（PMF）计算，研究RNA核苷酸与蛋白质氨基酸之间的相互作用景观。我们首先通过经典碱基配对分析表征核苷酸-核苷酸结合模式，观察到AMBER03ws和CHARMM36力场预测结果具有显著一致性。对不同核苷酸-核苷酸相互作用模式的进一步合理化涉及计算核糖-核糖、磷酸-磷酸以及RNA三级相互作用（如G-四链体形成）的PMF。我们还考察了盐浓度对这些相互作用的影响，发现随着离子强度增加，磷酸-磷酸结合的静电自排斥作用减弱。将分析扩展到氨基酸，我们首先基准测试AMBER03ws和a99SB-disp力场在描述成对氨基酸相互作用方面的性能，然后评估不同的核苷酸-氨基酸结合谱。我们的发现揭示了一组氨基酸——Lys和Arg（带正电）、Asp和Glu（带负电）以及Gln、Ser和Asn（极性残基）——始终与不同核苷酸的含氮碱基发生相互作用。这种结合主要由氢键介导，在某些情况下还涉及阳离子-π相互作用。此外，我们识别出与芳香族残基的强π-π堆积相互作用和磷酸-Arg接触是RNA-蛋白质凝聚体中凝聚体凝聚力的关键贡献因素。我们的综合分析提供了核苷酸-氨基酸相互作用的详细库，为粗粒化模型参数化提供定量见解，并加深我们对亚分子尺度上凝聚体自组装、核酸识别和相分离调控的理解。
